abstract_html: This note proves the conjecture of Kotěšovec on the factorial growth of the Matryoshka numbers (OEIS A177384), which arise from the combinatorics of the cosmohedron: the limit S = lim an/(n+4)! exists and is finite and positive, so an ∼ S n! n4, and S is certified to lie in an explicit interval of width below 10−9. The proof is elementary and independent of the resurgence approach, and the note was produced by an automated proof system. It is made available here following a suggestion of Professor Federico Ardila.

publication.title_html: The equality case of Ehrhart’s volume conjecture

abstract_html: On August 1, 2026, OpenAI released the report Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science, in which an internal version of its Astra model proved the inequality part of Ehrhart’s volume conjecture (1964), the eighth of the ten results. The conjecture concerns a very intuitive statement: an n-dimensional convex body whose barycenter is its unique interior lattice point has volume at most (n+1)n/n!. OpenAI proved that the volume indeed cannot exceed this number; which bodies attain the maximal volume — the equality part of the conjecture — was explicitly left open in the report.

We noticed that the core idea of OpenAI’s proof transports Fujita’s proof of the volume upper bound for K-semistable Fano varieties to convex geometry, and that the same paper of Fujita also settled the equality case on the Fano side: only the projective space attains the bound. The core of Fujita’s equality analysis is the Seshadri constant: equality forces the Seshadri constants to equal n+1 at every point, and the projective space attains this value exactly. The convex-geometric counterpart of the Seshadri constant is the lattice width: Seshadri = n+1 corresponds to lattice width at least n+1 in every integer direction, and the extremal simplex attains the bound exactly, its minimal lattice width being n+1. The plan of attack therefore centered on the width saturation.

This idea was given to our Danus system. Running with 8 agents, Danus carried out
            the first half of the proof along this correspondence; the second half has no
            complex-geometric counterpart, and Danus found it on its own. The total run took
            3 hours and 16 minutes. Combined with the result of OpenAI, both the
            inequality part and the equality part of Ehrhart’s volume conjecture are now
            resolved.

The manuscript has passed the author’s preliminary verification and is posted here
            as a note. A more detailed revision is in progress, and the note will be posted to
            arXiv upon its completion. Comments are very welcome.

html: We prove that every full-dimensional compact convex body in ℝn whose barycenter is its unique interior lattice point and whose volume is (n + 1)n/n! is a unimodular image of the simplex (n + 1)Δn − (1, …, 1). This resolves the equality case of Ehrhart’s volume conjecture, as a counterpart of the inequality part recently proved by OpenAI. The main result of this paper is obtained by generative AI, particularly GPT-5.6-sol, Fable 5, and the Danus system.

publication.title_html: Spectral gap, internality of relative commutants, and non-hyperlinear groups

abstract_html: This paper constructs a countable discrete group that is not hyperlinear. Equivalently, its group von Neumann algebra, with its canonical trace, does not embed into an ultrapower of the hyperfinite II1 factor, so Connes’ embedding problem has a negative answer for groups. The group is the generalized wreath product W = (⊕G/Γ Z/2) ⋊ G, where Γ = EL3(F2[x1, x2, x3]) and G = EL3(F2[x1±1, x2±1, x3±1]) ⋊ SL3(Z). It is one of the groups that Kun and Thom (arXiv:2608.06222) proved to be nonsofic, building on the first nonsofic group, found by OpenAI.

The new ingredient is a theorem on tracial ultraproducts of matrix algebras: the relative commutant of a finitely generated Kazhdan group in such an ultraproduct is itself an ultraproduct of finite-dimensional subalgebras of the same matrix algebras (Theorem 1.2 of the paper). This is a positive answer to the centralizer problem, that is, Open Problem 6.2(a) of Alekseev and Thom (arXiv:2608.05362). The second step of the argument (Theorem 1.3 of the paper: a Kazhdan group generated by a subgroup together with finitely many elements that conjugate this subgroup into itself normalizes the relative commutant of the subgroup) was proved earlier by Andreas Thom, conditionally on the centralizer problem, in his preprint A conditional construction of a nonhyperlinear group and the centralizer problem; the credit for it belongs to him (see the update of 20 September below). Danus ran with seven proof workers and found the proof in 7 hours and 11 minutes.

html: We construct a countable discrete group that is not hyperlinear. It is a wreath product built from a polynomial elementary subgroup of an explicit Laurent semidirect product, and a specified nonidentity product of two lamps vanishes under every homomorphism into a tracial matrix ultraproduct. We prove that commutants of finitely generated Kazhdan groups are internal in the original matrix dimensions, and that an internal subgroup commutant is normalized by a Kazhdan group generated by subgroup compressions. The argument constructs expanding matrix blocks from a quotient spectral gap, matches their full multiplicity algebras, and controls both matrix sizes and multiplicities under compression. The main result of this paper was obtained using the Danus system.

records.title_text: K-polystability of nilpotent orbit and Slodowy slice bases
abstract_html: This paper gives affirmative answers to both parts of Problem 23 in the list of Chenyang Xu and Ziquan Zhuang, Open problems in K-stability of Fano varieties, for every complex semisimple Lie algebra: the natural projective base of the normalization of a nonzero nilpotent orbit closure is K-polystable, and the natural projective base of each positive-dimensional component of a Slodowy slice of a nilpotent orbit closure, with the boundary given by the divisorial stabilizers of the Kazhdan action, is log K-polystable. Both statements come with weak Kähler–Einstein currents and with the equality case for all normal test configurations. Xu and Zhuang, with an appendix by Guenancia, had proved K-semistability of the orbit bases (arXiv:2606.02401) and recorded K-polystability for classical Lie algebras.

The proof constructs a homogeneous hyperkähler potential on the whole affine
            cone, not only on its smooth part. For matrix orbits and type-A slices the potential
            is the half-norm on a finite-dimensional hyperkähler quotient; a faithful
            representation pulls it back to an arbitrary semisimple Lie algebra, including the
            exceptional ones, and Kronheimer’s description of orbits and slices by
            trajectories makes the pullback compatible with all complex structures. A weighted
            descent then gives a weak Kähler–Einstein current of full mass on the
            projective base, and Berman’s theorem gives K-polystability.

The proof constructs global homogeneous potentials through framed hyperkähler comparisons, transports them in the correct natural coordinates, and checks weighted descent and affine products. abstract_html:
A klt del Pezzo surface of Picard number one over an algebraically closed field of
            characteristic three has at most seven singular points. Over the complex numbers the
            bound is four (Belousov), and Bernasconi’s example with seven singular points

records.title_text: Proof of the tropical Hodge conjecture for tropical abelian varieties
abstract_html: On a flat integral affine torus Vℝ/Γ with an arbitrary full-rank real period lattice Γ, in every dimension and every cycle dimension, the rational classes in the kernel of the Mikhalkin–Zharkov eigenwave are exactly the classes of finite balanced straight tropical cycles with rational, possibly negative, weights. In particular every rational tropical Hodge class on every tropical abelian variety is the class of such a cycle. Jell–Rau–Shaw had proved the codimension-one case with integral coefficients, and Amini–Piquerez the case of smooth projective tropical varieties admitting a rational triangulation, leaving open the tropical abelian varieties with irrational periods. The proof works with rational-faced polytopes with real offsets and needs no rational triangulation: complete endpoint moments and a Koszul lift over the period lattice, finite signed specialization and filling, a periodic polyhedral refinement, and a direct Stokes computation of the full marked class.

html: In every ambient dimension, for every full-rank real period lattice, and in every cycle dimension, we prove that the rational classes in the kernel of the eigenwave on a flat integral affine translation torus are exactly the classes of finite signed balanced straight tropical cycles with rational coefficients. In particular, every rational tropical Hodge class on every tropical abelian variety has such a representative. The proof uses complete endpoint moments, finite signed specialization and filling, periodic polyhedral realization, and a direct Stokes calculation of the full class. records.title_text: K-stability of prime Fano threefolds of genus ten and twelve
abstract_html: We prove that all smooth prime Fano threefolds of genus ten (family 1.9) are K-stable and that all smooth prime Fano threefolds of genus twelve (family 1.10) are K-semistable, and thereby solve Problem 10 of Xu–Zhuang’s open problem list on K-stability of Fano varieties, which asks to show that any smooth Fano threefold of Picard number one is K-semistable. For smooth prime Fano threefolds of genus twelve, we show that K-stability is equivalent to each special line intersecting another line and to the GIT-stability of the Hilbert scheme of lines as a plane quartic, that K-polystability is equivalent to the GIT-polystability of the quartic, and that each K-polystable one is isomorphic to a member of an explicit family over an open set of binary octics whose fiber over zero is the Mukai–Umemura threefold. We also disprove the original formulation of Donaldson’s conjecture, which predicts that such a threefold without a torus action is not K-polystable as soon as an anti-canonical divisor has a specific simple elliptic singularity, by an explicit K-stable example with finite automorphism group and with such a divisor, and we prove the prediction when the singular point is contained in a line.

records.title_html: Minimizers of the normalized volume on symplectic singularities
records.title_text: Minimizers of the normalized volume on symplectic singularities
abstract_html: We prove that the minimizer of the normalized volume on any symplectic singularity is, up to scaling, the valuation of a Kollár component whose log discrepancy equals the dimension of the singularity or half of it and whose log Fano pair is K-polystable. On the index-one cover of the Kollár component, the residue of the symplectic form is an orbifold contact form in the sense of reflexive differential forms, so that the Kollár component, with the orbifold structure given by the index-one cover, is a contact Fano orbifold. We thus solve Problem 25 of Xu–Zhuang’s open problem list on K-stability of Fano varieties and confirm the conjecture of Namikawa and Odaka that the minimizer is a multiple of a divisorial valuation.

records.title_html: Quaternionic structures on conical symplectic singularities
records.title_text: Quaternionic structures on conical symplectic singularities
abstract_html: We prove that the coordinate ring of any conical symplectic singularity with a grading induced by the minimizer of the normalized volume admits, for any torus of graded Poisson automorphisms, a quaternionic structure commuting with the maximal compact subgroup of the torus, and hence the weights of the torus on each graded piece, counted with multiplicity, are symmetric under negation. We also prove that the identity component of the group of graded Poisson automorphisms is reductive, that twisting the action on each graded piece by any Chevalley involution yields an isomorphic representation, and that the grading descended to a Hamiltonian reduction by such a torus is again induced by the minimizer of the normalized volume if the reduction, with the descended symplectic form, is a symplectic singularity. We thereby solve Problems 27, 28, and 29 and Parts (1) and (2) of Problem 30 in Xu and Zhuang’s list of open problems on K-stability of Fano varieties.
